newsitem.title: USA: SOCCER-NEW ENGLAND RALLY FOR 3-2 SHOOTOUT WIN.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-NEW ENGLAND RALLY FOR 3-2 SHOOTOUT WIN.

text.p: The New England Revolution rallied from a 2-0 deficit to record a 3-2 shootout victory over the Dallas Burn in Major League Soccer action on Sunday.

Imad Baba and Francis Okaroh scored in the tie-breaker, in which New England prevailed 2-1. Former Italian World Cup goalkeeper Walter Zenga made three saves in the shootout, on Mark Santel, Gerell Elliott and Ted Eck.

Mexican Damian Alvarez and Jason Kreis had given the Burn (8-7) a 2-0 lead after 27 minutes, but the Revolution (11-4) rallied behind Alejandro Farias (29th minute) and U.S. international defender Alexi Lalas (65th minute).

In Kansas City, Missouri, the Kansas City Wizards (9-5) rolled to a 6-1 triumph over defending champion D.C. United (11-4) in a confrontation of conference leaders. The loss, the worst in club history, broke United's six-game winning streak and a 22-game streak in which D.C. did not lose in regulation.
Preki and Frank Klopas finished with a goal and an assist apiece. Paul Wright, Mark Chung, Sean Bowers and Edmundo Rodriguez added goals. El Salvadoran Raul Diaz Arce scored United's lone goal.
In Denver, Colorado, the Colorado Rapids (8-8) won their third consecutive game to move into second place in the Western Conference, registering a 2-1 win over the Los Angeles Galaxy (4-10).

Chris Henderson and Paul Bravo scored first-half goals for the winners. Former U.S. international defender Paul Caligiuri, who made his Galaxy debut, found the back of the net with seven minutes remaining.
In Tampa, Florida, Colombian international Carlos Valderrama scored the first goal and created two others as the Tampa Bay Mutiny (7-7) registered a 3-1 win over the San Jose Clash (5-10).

Roy Lassiter, last season's scoring champion, and Trinidad & Tobaga native Evans Wise also tallied for the home team. Ronald Cerritos scored for San Jose, which played without injured U.S. national team striker Eric Wynalda.

In Columbus, Ohio, Brian McBride converted a controversial penalty kick with four minutes remaining as the Columbus Crew (7-8) snapped a six-game losing streak with a 2-1 victory over the New York/New Jersey MetroStars (5-10).
MetroStars defender Ezra Hendrickson was called for a handball in the penalty area.

A pair of U.S. internationals scored for each team, midfielder Mike Sorber for the MetroStars and defender Thomas Dooley, in his MLS debut, for the Crew. The MetroStars, who have dropped four straight matches, are winless in seven road games.
